stories.title: Hackers mint fake Bitcoin on bridge; only 15 BTC recovered for liquidity providers
stories.summary: Attackers exploited a bridge and minted a huge, fake supply of wrapped Bitcoin. The bridge recovered only 15 BTC. Liquidity providers who supplied real funds remain unpaid. The source does not name the bridge or give a total loss figure.
stories.whyItMatters: Bridge exploits keep draining real user funds even after operators claim a fix, and this case shows recovery can fall far short of the damage.
whatToWatch: A fuller loss and reimbursement report from the bridge operator
Any compensation plan for unpaid liquidity providers
questions: Which bridge or protocol was exploited?
How much real value did liquidity providers actually lose?

sources.title: Hackers mint trillions in fake Bitcoin, but 15 BTC bridge recovery leaves liquidity providers unpaid

stories.title: Revolut faces data-leak threats after phishing attack used a fake government email
stories.summary: Revolut said a phishing email that impersonated a government body exposed some customer data. The attackers now threaten to leak customer data every day. Revolut has not said how many customers are affected.
stories.whyItMatters: Revolut supports crypto trading for many users, so a breach and extortion threat raises the risk of targeted phishing against crypto holders.
whatToWatch: Whether the attackers carry out the daily leak threat
Revolut's formal notice to affected customers
Any regulatory response over the data exposure
questions: How many customers had data exposed?
What data types were taken — personal, financial, or crypto holdings?

sources.title: Revolut attackers threaten daily customer data leaks
Revolut says customer data exposed through fake government email

stories.title: Hodler's Digest: AI slowdown fears mark a big week for crypto
stories.summary: Cointelegraph's weekly Hodler's Digest rounds up a week it calls one of crypto's biggest, alongside fears of an AI slowdown tied to "swarm" concerns. As a digest, it summarizes multiple stories rather than one event.
stories.whyItMatters: A weekly roundup helps readers catch developments they may have missed, but it does not itself carry new facts to verify.
questions: What events made this 'crypto's biggest week ever'?
What are the 'swarm fears' behind the AI slowdown claim?

sources.title: Crypto’s biggest week ever? Swarm fears prompt AI slowdown: Hodler’s Digest

stories.title: Audited DeFi protocols still lost $885M to attacks outside their audit scope
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate analysis found DeFi protocols that had passed security audits lost a combined $885 million to attacks. The exploits fell outside what those audits covered. The finding points to limits of audits as a safety guarantee.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors often treat an audit as a safety signal; this shows audits miss large categories of real risk.
whatToWatch: Whether auditors widen their scope to cover the gaps found
Any new audit standards proposed in response
questions: Which attack types most often fall outside audit scope?
Over what time period was the $885M total measured?

sources.title: Audited DeFi protocols lost $885M to attacks that occurred completely outside their audit scopes

stories.title: Coinbase offers community banks a stablecoin bridge, built on its own infrastructure
stories.summary: Coinbase is giving community banks a way to connect to stablecoins. Coinbase supplies the underlying infrastructure itself. The move extends Coinbase's bank partnerships down to smaller regional banks.
stories.whyItMatters: If community banks adopt stablecoin rails through Coinbase, it could speed mainstream bank access to crypto payments and strengthen Coinbase's role as infrastructure provider.
whatToWatch: Which community banks sign on first
Regulatory reaction to bank-crypto infrastructure ties
questions: What fees does Coinbase earn from this infrastructure role?
Which stablecoin or stablecoins are involved?

sources.title: Coinbase gives community banks a stablecoin bridge while supplying infrastructure underneath

stories.title: Bots are scanning exposed Bitcoin payment servers for master admin keys
stories.summary: Security researchers found malicious bots actively probing publicly exposed Bitcoin payment servers. The bots search for master administrative keys. Theft of these keys could give attackers control over held funds.
stories.whyItMatters: Exposed payment infrastructure is a growing target, and stolen admin keys can lead straight to fund theft.
whatToWatch: Whether specific payment processors confirm they were targeted
Guidance on securing exposed servers
questions: How many servers are currently exposed?
Has any theft been confirmed so far?

sources.title: Malicious bots are actively probing exposed Bitcoin payment servers to steal master administrative keys

stories.title: Critical Bitcoin Lightning bugs exposed nodes to fund theft and restart failures
stories.summary: Researchers disclosed critical bugs in a Bitcoin Lightning Network implementation. The flaws could have let attackers steal funds or stopped nodes from restarting properly. The source does not say whether the bugs were exploited before disclosure.
stories.whyItMatters: Lightning is Bitcoin's main payments layer, so critical bugs there threaten a core piece of Bitcoin's payment infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Confirmation that affected Lightning implementations have shipped patches
Any reports of funds lost before the fix
questions: Which Lightning implementations were affected?
Were the bugs exploited in the wild before disclosure?

sources.title: Critical Bitcoin Lightning bugs exposed nodes to fund theft and restart failure

stories.title: Bitcoin slips below $77,000 ahead of a key technical test
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $77,000, setting up what CryptoSlate calls a key technical test at the start of the week. The report also links the move to warnings from unnamed AI industry leaders. The source gives no further detail on those warnings.
stories.whyItMatters: A break below a closely watched price level can shape short-term trader positioning, though single-day moves say little about the longer trend.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitcoin holds or breaks further below $77,000 early this week
Follow-up reporting on the AI leaders' warning
questions: Which AI leaders issued warnings, and about what?
What exact technical level does the 'Monday test' refer to?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s slide below $77,000 sets up a Monday tech test as AI leaders sound warning

stories.title: Bitcoin's 'oil risk' narrative extends into 2027 as IEA cuts supply outlook
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that the International Energy Agency again cut its oil supply outlook. The report links this to what it calls a Bitcoin oil-price risk running into 2027. It does not detail the mechanism connecting oil supply to Bitcoin price.
stories.whyItMatters: Energy costs affect mining economics, but readers should treat broad macro-correlation claims with caution absent clear supporting data.
whatToWatch: The IEA's next supply outlook update
Any data tying mining costs or Bitcoin price moves to oil supply
questions: What specific link does the report draw between oil supply and Bitcoin?
Is this about mining energy costs or a broader macro correlation?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s oil risk stretches into 2027 as IEA cuts supply outlook again

stories.title: Report claims 90% of DeFi trades are quietly routed to Wall Street market makers
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate analysis claims roughly 90% of DeFi trades end up routed to traditional Wall Street market makers behind the scenes. This would echo payment-for-order-flow patterns seen in traditional finance. The report's methodology and the platforms it covers are not detailed here.
stories.whyItMatters: If accurate, it challenges the assumption that DeFi trading avoids the intermediary dynamics found in traditional markets.
whatToWatch: Responses from any DeFi protocols named in the analysis
Whether other researchers confirm or dispute the 90% figure
questions: Which market makers and protocols were examined?
How was the 90% figure calculated?

sources.title: Why 90% of your DeFi trades are quietly being routed back to Wall Street market makers

stories.title: Cosmos network recovers from outage, but Ledger users still can't access ATOM
stories.summary: The Cosmos network came back online after an outage. Ledger wallet users, however, still cannot see or send their ATOM tokens. It is not clear whether the problem sits with Cosmos or with Ledger.
stories.whyItMatters: A wallet-level access failure after a network outage leaves users unable to manage funds even once the chain itself is stable again.
whatToWatch: A fix or statement from Ledger on ATOM visibility
Confirmation of what caused the original Cosmos outage
questions: Is the ATOM display issue a Ledger bug or a Cosmos-side problem?
How many users are affected?

sources.title: Cosmos is back online after outage, but Ledger users still can’t see or send their ATOM

stories.title: AI's 2026 slowdown dilemma: nationalize or decentralize?
stories.summary: CryptoSlate argues a 2026 AI slowdown is forcing a choice between nationalizing AI development or decentralizing it. The piece frames decentralization as an alternative path, likely including blockchain-based compute or coordination. The title alone gives no specific policy proposals.
stories.whyItMatters: If decentralized, crypto-linked infrastructure becomes a proposed alternative to state-controlled AI, that would open a new tie between crypto networks and AI compute.
whatToWatch: Which decentralized AI projects or proposals gain traction
Any government moves toward nationalizing AI infrastructure
questions: What does 'decentralize' mean here — blockchain compute, open models, or something else?
What is driving the described 2026 AI slowdown?

sources.title: Why AI faces an immediately difficult choice: Nationalize or decentralize – AI’s 2026 slowdown dilemma
